drafts.title: Experiences managing local LLMs with llama.cpp and Open WebUI instead of Ollama?
drafts.body: A user reported moving away from Ollama about a month ago while continuing to use Open WebUI as their frontend. Their inference runs on llama.cpp or ik_llama.cpp across Linux and Windows, with llama-swap handling model loading/unloading via a large config.yaml. This approach reportedly avoids Ollama’s model location and naming constraints, allowing direct downloads from Hugging Face into arbitrary folders. However, the original post doesn’t specify hardware or performance details, nor does it explain the config.yaml setup or challenges faced during transition. Has anyone else adopted a similar modular stack replacing Ollama? What practical tradeoffs did you find in terms of setup complexity, model management flexibility, or inference reliability? Any insights on configuring llama-swap effectively or integrating with Open WebUI would be helpful.
